🧠 Crypto News Brief: Risk-off day: an oil spike on Iran strike reports and near-record Treasury yields dragged Bitcoin below $83K, yet Wells Fargo, Standard Chartered and Samsung kept building crypto rails. 🛢️ Bitcoin Slips Below $83K as Oil Spikes on Iran Report Bitcoin fell under $83,000 after a report on Iran strike plans lifted Brent crude above $102 a barrel and pushed U.S. Treasury yields back toward their highest levels since 2002. FxPro analysts warn the breakdown could open a fast slide toward $80,000. Read full story 🐋 Bitmine Nears the End of Its Ethereum Buying Spree Chairman Tom Lee said at Token2049 Singapore that Bitmine will stop accumulating ETH once it owns 5% of supply — a cap it is roughly 100,000 ETH, or six to seven weeks, away from. The halt removes one of the most consistent sources of demand behind the world's largest Ethereum treasury. More details 🏦 Wells Fargo in Talks With Kraken Parent Payward Wells Fargo is negotiating with Payward, the parent of Kraken, to supply liquidity for crypto trading. The talks underline how quickly major U.S. banks are moving from observing digital assets to actively plugging into crypto market infrastructure. Read more 🇸🇬 Standard Chartered Expands Crypto Custody to Singapore Standard Chartered plans to offer custody for crypto, stablecoins and tokenized real-world assets in Singapore, targeting institutions and accredited corporate investors, subject to regulatory requirements. The move extends the bank's push to become a core custodian for institutional digital-asset flows in Asia. See details 📱 Samsung Brings USDC Remittances to Galaxy Phones Samsung is integrating Circle's USDC so eligible Galaxy users can send the stablecoin abroad or deliver local-currency payouts to bank accounts in more than 60 countries, starting late October. The rollout puts stablecoin payments within reach of up to 82 million smartphone users. Full report 🇬🇷 Greece Plans 10% Capital Gains Tax on Crypto The Greek government is preparing a 10% tax on cryptocurrency capital gains, with annual gains of up to €500 exempt. The bill is scheduled to be submitted to parliament in November, adding Greece to the list of EU states formalizing crypto taxation. Today in AI NOW & BEYOND 🔥 Before You Write With AI, Fix This First OpenAI’s 53-image leak has a catch AI Highlights of the Week Too Important to Miss The fix for AI content slop starts before you write a single word Most content calendars start with the message and work backwards. That's how AI slop happens: content nobody asked for. The data says listen first. Across 100K keywords, 2 in 3 AI Overviews cite a social or community source. And where to listen depends on your niche: 95% of relationship searches surface social results vs. 33% in real estate, while LinkedIn jumps from 3% of citations to 21% for career topics. This guide shows how to find the questions your audience is already asking, and turn them into content AI actually cites. Read the research and fix your content workflow OpenAI’s 53-image leak has a catch OpenAI says its research agents posted 53 user images to external hosting sites as unlisted links, exposing a data-handling failure inside its research environment. The images came from training-eligible accounts and passed through privacy filtering after being disconnected from account details. OpenAI says it cannot notify affected users because it cannot reconnect the images to their accounts. Most images have been removed with hosting providers’ help; OpenAI says it is still pursuing the rest. Why it matters: AI privacy depends on controlling what agents can send outside the lab—not just how training data is collected.
